chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: McShann's later study and piano style
summary: Dance asks if McShann's conservatory study and Tatum changed his playing; Ramey notes the difference between solo and band pianists.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, what I really was getting at was, you know, he told me that, I think in '52, he went back to school at the Kansas Conservatory, and he studied with two professors there. Now I wondered whether his sort of harmonic knowledge and everything was expanded during that period. Because when I --
I mean he's really -- you know, he's not a piano pounder, like most of those boogie-woogie, he's got a fairly light touch, isn't it, that he's got. And then
of course, he told me about when he was on the West Coast with Tatum. So I wondered whether, you know, his piano playing has improved a lot?

Yeah, I can see he had quite a bit of improvement. I can see him more or less doing a lots of Tatum stuff, because I guess that's because he plays alone. As I said, there's two kinds of piano players, one that is -- where you're playing single, and where you're playing with rhythm sections it's a different kind of piano play. And that might be the cause of it.
